institution_matches.title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion
institution_matches.overview: The authors use deep reinforcement learning with networks of abstract oscillators, representing spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 distinct quadrupedal gaits and associated locomotion styles (base height, ground clearance, foot offsets) across diverse challenging terrains, and a second policy that selects among these gaits to optimize user-specified criteria such as cost of transport, base stability, or joint smoothness. Within the learned repertoire and across different terrains, performance metrics, and velocities, each gait is optimal under at least one terrain-metric-velocity combination, and the framework adapts zero-shot to unseen gait couplings and styles, out-of-distribution terrains, and larger quadrupeds up to five times the training mass; with a simple pitch-tracking reward extension, the same gait couplings also support bipedal-mode locomotion.

institution_matches.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI), which augments vision-language-action policies for safety by constructing fallback targets that command stationary arms and consistent gripper states throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and jointly adapting the policy so it learns these alternative responses alongside original behaviors. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and BadLIBERO benchmarks show that SAFI enables policies to stop safely mid-execution: on evaluated LIBERO tasks, aggregate target success after unsafe-policy takeover is reduced to 1.3%, with no observed physical incidents or action saturation, while retaining high success on allowed tasks.

institution_matches.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose O²LaF, a latent-action learning framework that repurposes a single pretrained video diffusion transformer as a shared prior for both inverse dynamics (via a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries) and forward dynamics (via a causal, action-conditioned video generator), training them end-to-end through a compact action bottleneck while carefully controlling information access. Across navigation and robotic manipulation settings, O²LaF learns transferable latent actions from unlabeled videos, achieving state-of-the-art few-shot action probing performance and stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments compared to prior methods, and an extension using predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2 attains competitive results under the same framework.

institution_matches.title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents VG-Steer, a test-time policy steering method that transfers nuanced motion from successful in-distribution rollouts using object-relational distance pairs, combining these geometric abstractions with semantic cues from large vision and vision-language models to form a visual-geometric guidance signal that corrects existing manipulation policies under distribution shift. In simulation, VG-Steer effectively corrects flow-matching policies under pose and task-goal shifts, and in real-robot experiments it expands the region of the workspace where a frozen cable-placement policy succeeds—more than doubling success one grid step outside the training positions—and steers a single-task policy toward unseen target objects while largely eliminating object confusion.

institution_matches.title: Ferrofluid Shape Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes a deep model-based reinforcement learning framework that learns ferrofluid shape control policies directly from physical interaction, using visual observations to command currents to a single fixed electromagnet and drive the fluid toward prescribed transient geometries that may not be sustainable at equilibrium. In hardware experiments with a single electromagnet, the learned policies repeatedly achieve a range of target shapes, including polygons, asterisks, and pentominoes, demonstrating reliable control of transient ferrofluid configurations under limited actuation.

institution_matches.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which a frontier multimodal agent supplies action-level intents and a critic evaluates outcomes and failure modes against those intents to enable systematic, action-level analysis of direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. Action-level analysis using AgentRoboCritic finds that frontier agents can exhibit closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, robust semantic grounding in diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation, while still suffering from task-relevant physical bottlenecks such as grasping, alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Using a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions, the authors fine-tune the open-source critic Muse-Glimmer-30B, improving its failure-mode classification accuracy from 32.58% to 74.24%, thereby enabling lower-cost action-level evaluation.

institution_matches.title: Learning Ankle Exoskeleton Control for Reactive Standing Balance Through Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes a simulation-to-real framework that combines motion imitation and reinforcement learning on a muscle-driven neuromusculoskeletal model, trained from limited motion-capture data of a single subject, to develop an ankle exoskeleton controller that provides bilateral balance assistance using only inertial sensor measurements without explicit perturbation detection. When deployed onboard a bilateral ankle exoskeleton and tested on five healthy subjects unseen in training, the learned controller increased the maximum backward-translation perturbation magnitude tolerated without stepping by 11.8% and reduced peak center-of-mass displacement and velocity by 13.5% and 28.2%, respectively. Experimental results indicate that a controller trained using a single virtual human model can transfer measurable balance benefits to multiple real users, with individual benefits depending on baseline recovery strategies and body mass, suggesting that more diverse virtual humans could further improve effectiveness.

institution_matches.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that infers latent variables of a generative image model to match monocular inputs, while constraining optimization with a frozen 3D lifting network to ensure multi-view-consistent, non-degenerate 3D reconstructions. Across controlled synthetic and real-world tasks, Infer3D achieves higher out-of-distribution 3D reconstruction accuracy than feedforward networks trained on equal or larger datasets, particularly under unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. The authors propose an adaptive inference strategy that allocates more test-time computation to ambiguous out-of-distribution inputs and routes in-distribution inputs more efficiently, analogously to longer human processing times for confusing stimuli.

topic_matches.title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for gas source localization in indoor environments, in which a mobile robot incrementally reconstructs a spatially varying airflow field from onboard wind and gas measurements, then uses this field in a forward dispersion model to update a probabilistic belief over source locations. The framework explicitly accounts for spatial variation in the reliability of the reconstructed wind field and incorporates this uncertainty into the gas source belief update, using the resulting belief map to drive informative path planning. High-fidelity simulations and physical indoor experiments show that incorporating lightweight physical airflow models improves robustness of localization under spatially complex indoor airflow and enables more efficient exploration compared with approaches lacking such physical structure.

topic_matches.title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces TuringPAI, a family of on-device Physical AI models including TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation, built on a HybridViT-MLQ backbone with multi-scale latent queries that integrate spatial features and temporal history in a compact interface to language models. TuringPAI-VL, a 0.65B-parameter model trained with general vision-language data plus geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision, supports multimodal understanding and yields improved quantitative geometric perception relative to Qwen2-VL-2B, while serving as a shared initializer for downstream driving and manipulation policies. Under practical on-device constraints, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE autonomous driving metrics within 1.2% of a full-token HybridViT baseline and runs at 12 Hz on an NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, while TuringPAI-Embodied attains a 96.8% average success rate across four LIBERO suites, indicating strong task performance with compact models.

topic_matches.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
topic_matches.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications; Southeast University; Tsinghua University
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework that augments a frozen navigation policy with memory-guided adaptive reasoning by using retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback to determine how many cached waypoints to execute before requesting a new prediction, plus a bounded local correction step at termination without extra model calls. On the HM3D-OVON and R2R-CE embodied navigation benchmarks, CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% and 64.7%, respectively, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, and improves both success rate and success weighted by path length when normalized per model call. Across four real-world navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 task successes versus 14 for native execution while cutting model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%, demonstrating improved compute efficiency without retraining the underlying policy.

topic_matches.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that couples an embodied agent with a vision-language-action policy to autonomously discover, represent, and verify task-relevant tool affordances—functional regions and key geometric properties—by reconstructing teleoperated demonstrations in simulation, conducting autonomous experiments, and building a reusable library of affordance-extraction skills. During downstream training and inference, A$^2$-VLA conditions a $\\pi_{0.5}$ backbone on encoded functional-region features, enabling cross-tool trajectory retargeting for unseen tools based on the discovered affordances. In evaluation, A$^2$-VLA achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting and improves real-robot task success on three tool-use tasks by 30.7 percentage points over the unaugmented $\\pi_{0.5}$ baseline.

topic_matches.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
topic_matches.institution: Wuhan Huaweike Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.; Wuhan University
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces TipDex-VTLA, a vision–tactile–language–action policy that regulates execution-time action refinement by estimating visual action reliability via Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) and combining it with Tactile Anticipation and Correction during Execution (TACE), which compares predicted and measured tactile signals and gates bounded corrections to future actions. TipDex-VTLA is trained using data collected under normal lighting yet, when evaluated on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and the UniVTAC simulation benchmark, attains average full-task success rates of 87.5% under normal lighting and 73.8% under challenging unseen lighting conditions, outperforming several existing methods under visual perturbations.

topic_matches.title: Hindsight Self-Distillation: Teaching Robots to Act from the Present
topic_matches.institution: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Nanjing University; Primotion; Shenzhen University; Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes Hindsight Self-Distillation (HSD), a training method in which a teacher branch with access to both current and future camera frames and a student branch with only current frames share a visual encoder and action predictor, summarize images into compact feature sets, and train the student to match both the teacher’s denoised action predictions and visual summaries from noisy demonstrations. At deployment, HSD uses the student alone, encoding current images once and reusing their summaries across denoising iterations, and achieves average success rates of 98.50% on the LIBERO benchmark and 92.31% on RoboTwin 2.0, indicating strong performance in visuomotor manipulation tasks.

topic_matches.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
topic_matches.institution: Gamma Robotics; Institute of Artificial Intelligence (TeleAI), China Telecom; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; ShanghaiTech University; Zhejiang University
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes ECHO, an in-context humanoid behavior foundation model that first learns a general behavior prior via Mixed and Annealed Sampling, then uses Context Representation and Residual Adaptation to derive dynamics-specific residual corrections from interaction histories without test-time parameter updates. In extensive experiments across diverse motions and physical conditions, ECHO outperforms all baseline methods, indicating improved environment-specific precision over prior BFMs that do not explicitly separate behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. On Unitree G1 hardware, ECHO enables whole-body teleoperation for extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, as well as payload-adaptive manipulation and whole-body control, demonstrating transfer of its learned control strategy to a real humanoid platform.

topic_matches.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces passage-conditioned navigation for wheeled-legged robots, which stores each taught stair or ledge crossing as an event and, during replanning, enforces an entry gate that makes the robot turn or back up and retry if its approach deviates by more than 10 cm or 10° from the taught crossing, without requiring a robot model or additional training. In experiments with localization noise and unchanged path, gait schedule, and sensing, passage-conditioned navigation increases the share of disturbed ledge crossings that end within 10 cm and 10° of the taught crossing from 24.1% to 88.6%, and in contact simulation prevents any falls in 180 disturbed stair climbs (versus 9 falls when stored approach direction is ignored) while enabling a robot pushed 1.2 m off course to rejoin the route and finish with an average endpoint offset of 0.14 m (1.10 m without rejoining). Deployed on a real wheeled-legged robot in competition over 271 m of multi-obstacle terrain with 7.0 m elevation change, the method completes all six runs fully autonomously and secures third place at the 2026 Global Open-source AI Challenge, being the only finalist in its task to finish without human intervention.

topic_matches.title: From Sequence to Space: Explicit Spatial Belief with Vision-Language Distillation for Active Geo-Localization
topic_matches.institution: National Space Science Center, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents EAGLE, an Explicit spatial-belief Agent for Geo-Localization and Exploration, which offline-trains a teacher-conditioned Swin branch and a context-free Swin student on randomly masked aerial mosaics using reconstruction and uncertainty supervision; the student additionally distills stop-gradient predictions from a Qwen2.5-VL-7B-conditioned teacher, then alone predicts cell-level aerial embeddings and uncertainty from partial observations to build a spatial belief tensor for a CNN actor-critic policy. After distillation, EAGLE discards the VLM, cached context, and teacher-attention branch, and uses a frozen student plus a compact CNN trained with PPO to perform active geo-localization from partial aerial observations and aligned goal embeddings without any vision-language model or cached visual tokens at inference. EAGLE achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 78.1% on MASA, 76.4% on xBD zero-shot transfer, and 76.8% on the MM-GAG zero-shot aerial-goal split for active geo-localization tasks involving aerial, ground, and text goals.

topic_matches.title: Close&Safe: Maximal Task Preservation for Redundant Manipulators via C-Space Boundary Detour
topic_matches.institution: Indian Institute of Science (IISc); Indian Institute of Technology Ropar; New York University Abu Dhabi
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes Close&Safe, a trajectory-repair method for redundant manipulators that decouples tracking from avoidance by following the nominal end-effector trajectory exactly wherever feasible and only altering the motion over intervals obstructed by unforeseen obstacles, sampling the configuration-space obstacle boundary in a corridor around the nominal and finding a minimal-deviation detour that rejoins the nominal at the earliest feasible configuration. Across diverse simulated obstacle configurations, physical experiments on a Franka manipulator, and ablations of algorithmic components, Close&Safe produces collision-free trajectory repairs with localized task modification, recovering 52.4–78% of the original nominal trajectory in both simulation and hardware evaluations.
